title: Jonathan ben Aryeh
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Yalkut Tehillim, remez 859: “said … said in the name of Rabbi Yohanan”; but Hyman calls this a printer’s error and insists that one must read “ben Meria,” as in the Yerushalmi, Peah, beginning of chapter 1.

notes.text: The source repeats אמר (“said”) across the line break. Hyman proposes ben Meria instead of ben Aryeh.

The saved whole YalkutNach859 scalar has Rabbi Yonatan ben Aryeh בשם Rabbi Yochanan, with no doubled אמר at that clause; the whole Guggenheimer Peah1:1 scalar instead has Rabbi Yochanan bar Meria בשם Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman insists on ben Meria and calls the other reading a printer’s error; the body attributes that claim without softening its force. The doubled supplied אמר remains visible, and Yonatan/Yochanan plus ben/bar remain disclosed differences. These digital parallels do not prove a print duplication or deletion history.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume II, printed p. 701, confirms both the heading Jonathan ben Aryeh and the repeated אמר (“said”) across the line break. The English preserves that repetition. The consulted Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 859 names Rabbi Yonatan ben Aryeh in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, whereas Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1 names Rabbi Yochanan bar Marya in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. The first name and ben/bar therefore differ as well. Hyman’s insistence on the correction remains his own judgment; the comparison does not establish an identity between the named sages.
